candidates.source_title: Woman Surprised While Using Phone Outdoors
candidates.modern_context: Smartphone attention collides with a passing e-scooter in an ordinary street; scrolling distraction is visible in the actual footage.
candidates.motion_observation: 0.00–1.67s: woman looking down at green smartphone while walking; around 2.08s a scooter rider crosses close to camera; 2.50–3.33s she jolts backward with both hands raised and looks after him; 4.08s turns back toward her phone; blunt cut resets to oblivious scrolling.
candidates.style_review: Ordinary street, moving handheld framing, awkward closeness and an unpolished interruption read at card size. This is staged stock footage, not an asserted candid accident.
candidates.recommendation_reason: Physical interruption is readable silently and has more than one defensible reading; the modern device and scooter are in the action itself.

candidates.title: One more quick question.
candidates.modern_context: Laptop overload as an original reaction to the always-on workday. Microsoft’s June 17, 2025 Work Trend Index follow-up describes meetings, messages and notifications fragmenting work; this source clip predates the report and does not document its participants or a visible notification.
candidates.situation: Digital work / meeting and notification overload
candidates.shelf_life: topical framing on evergreen digital-work footage
candidates.motion_observation: 0.00s laptop focus; 0.42–1.25s removes glasses and rubs face; 1.67s exasperated hand gesture; 2.08–2.92s double facepalm/head slump; 3.75–4.42s chin in hands before abrupt return to focused starting pose.
candidates.style_review: Flat office scene and readable facepalm. Cleaner, more staged composition than preferred candid lo-fi direction; retain as an owner-review option with this caveat, not as an approved style benchmark. Compression alone does not resolve that limitation.
candidates.recommendation_reason: The modern overload interpretation works, but owner should decide whether this clean stock staging is too polished; no notification or video call is actually visible.
hypotheses: The quick call has a sequel.

candidates.title: We said one casual game.
candidates.modern_context: Headset, microphone and multiplayer PC setup frame an exaggerated gaming celebration. Contemporary online gaming culture; no claim that this is footage of a named tournament or a recent event.
candidates.mechanism: Petty stakes treated as epic; sudden reversal from concentration to celebration
candidates.motion_observation: 0.00–0.83s leans forward in headset concentrating on PC; 1.25–2.08s face opens into shout/laugh; 2.50–3.75s both fists rise while leaning back; 4.17–4.92s smiles and begins to settle; abrupt reset to keyboard focus.
candidates.style_review: Close awkward vertical crop, candid-like outburst and visible practical gaming LEDs. Staged stock with colored lighting; no cinematic camera move or added premium treatment.
candidates.recommendation_reason: The visible sudden reaction supplies the joke without a caption; headset/PC context is immediately modern, while achievement, relief and competitive overreaction remain defensible alternatives.
hypotheses: One tiny win after a terrible evening.
Everyone survives the supposedly casual match.
